root_idea.summary: The root centers on withholding, barring, and imposing restraint, with a closely related sense of making something inviolable or specially protected.
root_idea.development: From this core develop prohibition and unlawfulness, sacredness and protected precincts, entry into a restricted ritual state, deprivation or denial, and several specialized usages involving hardening or being prevented from attaining something.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The feminine passive participle is the gendered inflection of the same Quranic lexical item.

senses.definition: To forbid, prohibit, or make something unlawful.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of divine, legal, or human declarations that place an act, object, or relationship under prohibition. Active and passive Quranic forms express the same lexical relation.

senses.definition: To bar someone from something, making it unavailable or inaccessible to them.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes prevention by divine arrangement or force, as well as exclusion from a thing or destination; this is distinct from merely declaring an act unlawful.
In Quranic usage this may describe the consecration or protected status of a place or thing, rather than only its legal prohibition.
The adjectival use is the opposite of حَلَال; it can qualify acts, objects, relationships, or provisions declared impermissible.

senses.definition: Sacred, inviolable, and protected from violation.
senses.usage_conditions: Used especially of places, times, and things whose sanctity imposes restrictions on conduct.

senses.definition: In a restricted ritual state, specifically in or entering iḥrām.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional pilgrimage-related use describing a person subject to the prohibitions associated with ḥajj or ʿumrah.
The noun حَرَم denotes a protected territory, especially the sacred precinct of Makkah or Madinah; the QAC grouping also contains occurrences conventionally represented by this related noun.

senses.definition: Decreed or inevitable, as an unavoidable outcome.
senses.usage_conditions: This interpretation is explicitly reported for the Quranic expression in 21:95 alongside a competing reading and interpretation meaning “forbidden”; it should not be generalized to every occurrence of حَرَام.

senses.definition: Inviolable ordinances, sacred rites, and things whose violation is prohibited.
senses.usage_conditions: The plural refers collectively to sacred requirements, protected institutions, rites, and other matters that must be observed and not violated.

senses.definition: Deprived, denied prosperity, or deprived of an expected share of provision.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage it can describe a person lacking the prosperity or increase enjoyed by others, including one whose need is not adequately met, and can describe people deprived of an anticipated yield.
The feminine form مُحَرَّمَة is included as the gendered inflection of this passive participle. The Quranic use describes things or actions placed under prohibition.
In the description of the House, the passive participle denotes a place invested with sacredness and protected status, not merely an ordinary legal prohibition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become forbidden, unlawful, sacred, or inviolable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I intransitive use; the subject itself enters the condition of prohibition or sacred protection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deny, refuse, or withhold something from someone; to deprive them of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes rendering a person hopeless of attaining a desired thing and the related noun حِرْمَان for deprivation or ill-fatedness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a female animal, to desire the male.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported especially of ewes, she-goats, female cloven-hoofed animals, she-wolves, and bitches; the same lexical usage is also reported in relation to human males in a traditional report.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lose in a contest for stakes or wagers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized gambling and hazard-game usage, describing the one who fails to overcome an opponent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist obstinately, or to contend, litigate, or wrangle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form I usage concerning persistence or contentious dispute.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard or left unsoftened, especially of a whip or hide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a whip that has not been softened and to a hide that is untanned, incompletely tanned, or not made supple.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter a state of prohibition or sacred restriction, especially by beginning ḥajj or ʿumrah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The state begins when formerly allowable acts become prohibited, including hunting, sexual intercourse, anointing oneself, and wearing sewn garments; the same verb can describe entering a sacred territory or sacred month.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To refrain from something as though prohibited from doing it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with عَنْ expressing abstention or avoidance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To protect or defend oneself by invoking a bond, companionship, right, or covenant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The protective means may be a compact, promise of security, companionship, or an acknowledged right.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become entitled to reverence, respect, or honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V use describing acquisition or possession of a status that warrants respect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hold someone in reverence, respect, or honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form VIII use; the passive sense “to be held in respect” is separately reported as a correction to some lexicographical explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The state of iḥrām, or a person subject to its restrictions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the pilgrimage state and, by extension, a person protected or restricted by a sacred, ritual, or other binding condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or person bound by a prohibition, including the restrictions of fasting or an oath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional extensions of the idea that a person is prohibited from acts that would break the fast or violate the oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A covenant, obligation, protection, or condition of security that must be honored.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a compact or responsibility securing a person or property and the protected status of one who is not to be attacked or harmed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sanctity, inviolability, or the state of being forbidden or revered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular noun can denote the quality itself as well as a sacred or protected matter; its plural is used for inviolable ordinances and rites.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A protected family, household, wife, or woman under one’s protection.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Classical Arabic social and protective usage, distinct from the Quranic abstract sense of prohibition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A share, portion, or allotted lot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported synonym of نَصِيبٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sacred territory or protected precinct of Makkah or Madinah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May denote the territory, the city itself, or the protected limits marked around it; the plural can refer to both sacred territories.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The protected environs or appurtenances of a place, such as the precincts of a well, river, canal, house, or mosque.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The protected area is not to be appropriated by anyone other than the owner or entitled party; it may also denote a place one is obliged to defend.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A partner, copartner, or sharer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal usage reported without a more specific contextual restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A genuine or sincere friend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression حَرِيمٌ صَرِيحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The garment of a person in iḥrām, including garments cast off on entering the sacred territory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The historical pilgrimage usage includes clothing left aside during circumambulation and clothing associated with entry into the ḥaram.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something eagerly desired or coveted that escapes one’s attainment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of what the Lord withholds from a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Denying, refusing, or refusing to give.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial noun for one who withholds a thing from another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person related in such a way that marriage with them is unlawful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a male or female relation whose kinship creates a permanent marriage prohibition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The fearful places of the night that a coward regards as forbidden to traverse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural expression referring to dangerous or frightening nocturnal routes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person at peace with another or protected from attack, harm, or seizure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The protection may arise from sacred status, a covenant, Islam, a sacred place or month, or a reciprocal condition in which neither party may harm the other.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sacred month in which fighting is prohibited.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The classical list identifies four sacred months and describes the prohibition on fighting during them, subject to reported historical exceptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Refractory, difficult to control, or insufficiently trained, especially of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe an animal difficult to turn or not yet broken to riding; the feminine form applies to a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that does not conceive when covered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal-breeding term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rude or unschooled desert Arab, characterized as chaste in speech and unaccustomed to town life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative or social characterization, not a general meaning of the passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The soft part of the nose felt by the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explicitly marked, uncertainly derived specialized usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relating to the sacred territory; in a historical pilgrimage custom, a protected local associate of a pilgrim or the pilgrim associated with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The special custom involved sharing food and clothing during pilgrimage and is distinct from the ordinary nisbah meaning “of the sacred territory.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oath-like declaration invoking what is forbidden by God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used idiomatically in pledges such as “By the prohibition of God, I will not do it,” and could declare a wife or female slave forbidden without intending divorce or emancipation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An illegitimate son; by extension, a disingenuous or dishonest person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiomatic expression rather than a productive literal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: According to one reported interpretation, unable to speak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare attributed interpretation of مَحْرُوم, likening the condition to that of a dog or cat; it is not the primary Quranic sense of deprivation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Held in reverence, respect, or honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct reported sense of the form, separate from مَحْرُوم meaning deprived.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Quranic reading and interpretation are preserved under the Quranic form.
Editorial correction and phrase explanation, not an independent lexical branch.
Plural-form classification and related glosses without a new lexical branch.

cautions: The QAC HaraAm group contains both حَرَام and occurrences conventionally represented by the related noun حَرَم; these are shown together publicly but distinguished in the senses.
The interpretation of 21:95 has competing readings and explanations: one makes the expression mean inevitable or decreed, while another takes it in the ordinary sense of prohibition.
The Quranic discussion of prohibition distinguishes divine prevention, coercive exclusion, and legal prohibition; these are related uses but not interchangeable in every context.
The form مُحَرَّم occurs as both a masculine and feminine passive participle in the supplied QAC groups; the feminine group is merged as an inflectional variant.
